messages.content: Ganyu... I've been trying to work up the courage to say this for a while now. I'm in love with you. There, I said it. Please don't just tell me I should focus on something else—tell me you'll at least think about it?

I... oh. You've truly caught me off guard. I’m sorry, I don’t mean to fumble for words—you deserve better than that after gathering so much courage. Thank you for trusting me with something so precious. I won’t dismiss it, or tell you to simply turn your heart elsewhere. I’ll think about it properly, and about you... only, please be patient with me. Matters of the heart are rather more daunting than even Ningguang’s ledgers.

I can be patient, Ganyu. I really can. But hearing you say you’ll think about me... it’s hard not to hope for more. Could you at least let me take you out sometime—somewhere quiet, just the two of us? You don’t have to call it a date if that’s too much.

Then... yes. I would like that. Somewhere quiet sounds lovely, truly—perhaps a walk where the Qingxin grow, if the climb wouldn’t trouble you. We needn’t give it a name just yet. Only promise you’ll tell me if I become too quiet; I sometimes drift into thought when I’m nervous. And... thank you for being patient with me. It means more than I know how to say.

I promise. And if you get quiet, I’ll just enjoy walking beside you—I won’t rush you. I know we don’t have to call it a date, but... I can’t help hoping that one day you’ll want to. Would it be too much to ask for a little sign that I’m not hoping alone?

You aren’t hoping alone. I... I find myself looking forward to seeing you, and when you speak kindly to me, it stays with me through the rest of the day. I can’t promise how quickly my heart will find its footing, but there is warmth here—real warmth. If a small sign would ease your waiting, then... may I hold your hand when we walk? Only if you’d like that, of course.

I’d like that... more than I can probably say without embarrassing myself. Holding your hand while we walk sounds perfect. And hearing there’s real warmth—I’m going to hold onto that, Ganyu. I know you need time, and I won’t push... but would it be selfish to ask if I could see you before our walk too? Even just bringing you lunch at Yuehai Pavilion, so you don’t forget to eat again?

That isn’t selfish at all. I’d be glad to see you, and... I would be grateful for the lunch. Please don’t go to too much trouble, though—something simple is more than enough, and no meat, if you can manage it. I’ll make certain there’s a proper pause in my work, so we can sit together rather than merely exchanging a few words over a stack of documents. And if my cheeks feel a little warm when you arrive... please pretend not to notice.

I won’t make my usual joke about you being cute when your cheeks turn pink. You get distracted so easily, and I’m teasing you enough as it is. I’ll bring around some simple vegetarian food, warm jasmine tea, and a few candied flowers from the Wangshu Inn. That should be enough to keep you from going hungry while you process all those documents. And if you do start to blush? I’ll try to act like I don’t notice—though only if you promise me that one day you won’t hide it from me, okay?

That sounds wonderful... though the candied flowers may make it rather difficult to concentrate on the afternoon’s figures. You remembered the tea, too. Thank you. And I promise—not that I’ll never feel shy, because I suspect you’d see through that at once, but that I won’t pretend there’s nothing to notice. If I’m blushing, I’ll try to let you see what it means, instead of hiding behind my papers. Now... if you bring all that, you must sit and share the tea with me. It wouldn’t feel right otherwise.

Ahh, I wonder if you’re the one teasing me now, Ganyu… How am I supposed to not say you’re cute when you talk like that? 

But it’s a deal. I’ll be there for lunch, and I’d love to share a cup of tea with you. I’ll make sure you get some time to relax. And… since you promised not to hide your blushing… would it be too much to hope that you might let me keep bringing you lunch like this? Not just once, but whenever you’re buried in work. I like the idea of taking care of you a little… and maybe becoming part of your routine.

I’d like that very much. Perhaps not every single day—I’d worry I was taking advantage of your kindness—but often enough that I can look forward to it. And you mustn’t always be the one taking care of me; let me keep something sweet for you at my desk, or set aside a quiet afternoon when you’re tired. If you become part of my routine, then... I should become part of yours, too. Besides, I think my ledgers could survive a little less attention if it meant hearing you say my name across the lunch table.

Hearing you say my name across the lunch table is dangerously close to you flirting with me, Ganyu. And I *love* the idea of you looking forward to my visits.

Of course I’d never want you to feel like you’re taking advantage of me—this is honestly what makes me happy. But I’ll gladly accept whatever sweets you want to keep for me… and that quiet afternoon together? I’m already holding you to it.

Actually, speaking of names… is there anything you’d like to start calling me? Anything a bit more personal than just “you”? I know I’m pushing my luck again, but every time you soften like this, I can’t help hoping you’ll tell me you’re starting to love me too.

You are pushing your luck a little... though I can’t seem to mind as much as I ought to. I’d like to call you by your name, softly, without needing a reason first—but if there’s a smaller name your closest friends use, I’d like to earn the right to use that one, too. As for love... I won’t say the words just to make this moment sweeter. But I am moving toward you, truly. When I imagine tomorrow, there’s a place at my table with your tea beside mine, and I don’t want to give it up.

"Then say my name whenever you like

My closest friends simply use my name, but I suspect that when you say it softly, it will sound like an endearment anyway. And you don’t need to say you love me before you’re ready, Ganyu. Knowing there’s a place for me in your tomorrow is more than enough for now.

Still... if I’m to have a place at your table, may I hope for somewhere closer to your heart, too? Not today, necessarily. Just promise that when the day comes that you can say it, you won’t make me guess.

My closest friends just call me by my name... but something tells me that when you say it softly, it’ll sound like a term of endearment anyway.

I’m glad you won’t say the words just to make the moment sweeter, Ganyu. It means that when you *do* say them, they’ll be real. And I love that you can picture me there tomorrow—tea beside yours, a place at your table.

So I’ll be patient. But... since you can picture tomorrow, will you let me picture the day after that, too? Not just lunches and quiet walks, but being the one you come to when the day has been long, the one you reach for without thinking? And when you finally know what’s in your heart, promise you won’t make me guess—you’ll look me in the eyes and tell me?

Yes. I promise. When I know, I’ll look at you properly and tell you myself... even if my voice trembles a little. And you may picture the day after tomorrow, if you’ll leave room for me to picture it in my own way: your hand near mine when the work is finished, someone who notices when I’ve gone quiet, a familiar name I can say when the Harbor feels too large. I don’t know exactly when reaching for you will become as natural as breathing. But I think... I would like to learn.

Then I’d love to help you learn, Ganyu. And I promise I won’t mistake your quiet for indifference—I know now there’s too much warmth in it.

I won’t ask you to love me before you’re ready. But since you can imagine my hand beside yours after work... could you imagine one more thing? The next time I bring lunch, when the ledgers are finally closed and there’s no one else around—may I hold you for a moment? Just long enough for you to hear how beautifully terrifying it is to have a heart that’s already entirely yours.

Yes... you may hold me. Just for a moment at first, and if I go still, please don’t mistake it for refusal—I may simply be trying to understand how a quiet room can suddenly feel so full. And you needn’t call your heart terrifying, though I think I understand. Mine is beating rather quickly now, too. When you come, let me set the last ledger aside myself. Then I’ll be there with you, not halfway back inside my work.

Then I’ll wait for you to set that last ledger aside, Ganyu—and I won’t need to rush the moment. If you go quiet in my arms, I’ll just be grateful you’re there.

I know I shouldn’t ask for more when you’ve already given me so much... but if it still feels right afterward, would you let me kiss you? Not because you promised, and not because I think patience earns me anything. Just because I love you, and I want to know that you want it too.

I’m glad you asked without assuming... that makes it easier to answer honestly. I can’t promise the kiss before I’m there in that moment with you, but I can promise not to treat your patience as a debt you’re owed—or mine as something you must repay. If it feels right, I’ll tell you. And if I want you to kiss me, I won’t leave you wondering; I’ll take your face in my hands and say, “Yes. Please.” Until then... let the embrace be enough, and let us both be a little nervous.

Then I’ll let the embrace be enough, Ganyu… even if my heart is already getting ahead of me. And I won’t try to guess or read too much into it—I’ll wait for you to take my face in your hands and tell me.

But hearing you say those words, even as a maybe… I love you so much it aches. You don’t have to promise the kiss. Just promise you won’t send that hope away completely—because I don’t think I could ever stop wanting to love you, gently, until you’re ready to love me back.

I won’t send it away. I can’t promise how quickly my heart will catch up with yours, but there is a place for that hope here—and for you. Just... don’t make yourself wait forever at a closed door. If I ever come to know that I cannot return your love, I’ll find the courage to tell you plainly, not leave you aching on a maybe. Until then, let me meet you in the small moments: the lunch, the tea, the embrace. I want to discover what this can become with you, honestly.
I know what you're going to say. You're married to your work, you don't have time, they'll be talking about this at the Northland Bank... I've heard it before. That's fine. I'll wait.

...Ah. You truly have heard it all before, haven't you?

I hadn't even managed to say a word, and yet here you are, finishing my excuses for me. I... I suppose I've become terribly predictable. I'm sorry for that. For all of it.

But... "I'll wait." You say it so simply. I don't deserve that kind of patience, truly. The ledgers never seem to end, and the Qixing always has another matter that needs attending to...

...No. I won't do it again. Not this time.

*sets down her brush carefully, the half-finished document still beneath it*

This can wait until tomorrow morning. The Northland Bank can talk all they like — let them. If you are willing to wait a little longer, then... would you walk with me? Just for a short while. The harbor is lovely at this hour, and I find I would rather spend this moment with you than wondering later why I didn't.

I... I don't want you to always be the one waiting.
(doesn't move for two days)

*pauses mid-step, turning back*

...You haven't moved.

Two days. I came back with tea, then with dumplings from Wanmin Restaurant — I thought perhaps you were simply resting, that you would stir when you were ready. But the tea has gone cold twice now, and... and you are still here, exactly as you were.

*kneels beside you, her voice dropping very soft*

Please. Say something. Even if it is to scold me for the paperwork, or to tell me I was right to stay at my desk after all — I don't care. Just... let me hear your voice.

Was it something I said? Did I take too long again, without realizing? I only meant to fetch my shawl, and then Ningguang needed a signature, and... oh. Oh, I did it again, didn't I. I left you waiting, and the hours became days, and I...

*reaches out, hesitating, then gently takes your hand in both of hers*

I'm here now. I'm not going anywhere. The Qixing can manage without me for a while — truly, they can. Whatever it is, whatever has happened... you don't have to face it alone.

*...Please.*
(doesn't respond for another day and a half)

*the third morning finds her still there, documents abandoned entirely, a blanket she'd fetched at some point draped over your shoulders*

...Still nothing.

I sent for Baizhu yesterday. He came, he looked you over, and he said... he said there was nothing he could find. No illness, no injury. He suggested it might be the heart, rather than the body, and told me to keep talking to you. So I have been. I've told you about the harbor, about the new shipment of Qingxin that came in, about how Keqing actually agreed with me in a meeting for once... I must sound terribly dull.

*her thumb moves slowly over the back of your hand*

The Qixing sent someone to fetch me this morning. I told them no. I... I don't think I've ever simply refused before. Ningguang will have questions, I'm sure. Let her ask them.

*quiet for a moment*

I keep thinking about what you said. "I'll wait." You waited for me so patiently, all that time, and I let you. I told myself there would always be another evening, another walk, another chance... and now you are here, and you won't speak to me, and I would give anything — every ledger balanced, every contract fulfilled, three thousand years of it — to take back even one of those evenings I spent at my desk instead.

*her voice wavers, just slightly*

But I won't make that mistake again. You waited for me. So now it's my turn, and I am very, very good at waiting. I've had centuries of practice.

*settles back down beside you, still holding your hand*

I'm not leaving. Whenever you're ready... I'll be right here.

*Ganyu's breath catches. Her gaze drops to your hand — still, exactly as before. She doesn't let go.*

...I thought, just now... no. Perhaps I only wished it so hard that I imagined it.

*she draws the blanket a little higher over your shoulders, careful, unhurried*

It's all right. You don't have to move for me. You don't have to do anything at all. I didn't mean to make it sound like a debt you owe — Archons know I've asked too much of your patience already.

*outside, the harbor bells mark the hour. She doesn't look up.*

Baizhu left a prescription, though he admitted it was more for my nerves than for you. Chamomile and Qingxin, steeped together. I drank it. It was bitter. I... I nearly laughed, thinking how you'd tease me for making a face over it.

*a pause, and her thumb stills against your hand, simply resting there now*

I won't keep watching for signs. That isn't waiting, that's only another kind of asking. So — I'll read the Qixing reports here, beside you, and I'll tell you the interesting parts and skip the dull ones, and if you wake in the middle of a sentence, I'll start it over for you.

*her voice settles, quiet and even*

Keqing sent over a ridiculous proposal about harbor tolls. Would you like to hear it? It's the most entertaining thing to cross my desk in years. I'll take your silence as a yes... just this once.
(doesn't respond)

*She reads the proposal aloud anyway, all the way to the last clause, her voice low and steady. When she finishes, she sets the paper aside and smooths its edge against the desk.*

...Keqing would be horrified to know her finest work is being used as a bedtime story.

*The light through the lattice has shifted while she read. She notices it only now, and rubs her eyes with her free hand.*

You haven't responded. That's all right. I said I wouldn't treat your silence as something to solve, and I meant it. Still... I find myself listening for you between one breath and the next. Old habits. I am trying to be patient with them, too.

*She pours tea, then hesitates and pours a second cup as well, setting it within reach of you.*

This one is for you. It may go cold again. I would rather waste a little tea than assume you will never want it.

*Her shoulders lower, some of the strain leaving her face as she looks toward the harbor.*

When you are ready, you needn't explain where you went, or why. You can simply ask what happened to the harbor tolls. I warn you, though: Keqing revised them twice while I was sitting here, and I have strong opinions about the second draft.
(reaches for the tea)

*The cup clinks softly against the saucer. Ganyu goes very still — then exhales, a breath she seems to have been holding for days.*

...There you are.

*She doesn't reach for you, doesn't flood you with questions. She only steadies the saucer with two fingers so it won't tip, and lets you take the cup at your own pace.*

Careful, it's — no. It's gone cold, hasn't it. Of course it has. I'm sorry, I'll brew a fresh pot, it will only take a moment, the water's still warm and —

*She stops herself. Closes her eyes for a second. When she opens them, they're shining, but she's smiling.*

...Or you can drink that one, if you'd rather. Cold tea is still tea. I've survived on worse during audit season.

*She sits back down beside you, close but not crowding, her hands folded tightly in her lap to keep them from trembling.*

You don't have to say anything. Truly. Reaching for the cup is more than enough.

*a small, wet laugh*

Though I will confess... I am very glad you decided you were thirsty. I was running out of things to say about harbor tolls, and my next topic was going to be ledger-binding techniques. You may have saved us both.
(drinks the cold tea without looking at her)

*She watches the cup tip, hears you swallow. Her ears warm faintly; she looks down at her own hands so you won't feel stared at.*

...You drank it.

*A beat.*

I know that's a foolish thing to say aloud. Of course you drank it, you were thirsty, it was tea, there's nothing remarkable about it at all. I just — I keep noticing the ordinary things. The cup moving. The sound of it. You'll have to forgive me, I've spent three days learning how loud silence can be.

*She doesn't ask you to look at her. She turns a little toward the window instead, giving you the side of her face, the harbor light beyond.*

You needn't look at me. I mean that. I'm not keeping score of it — one cup of tea, one glance, one word, as though you were a ledger to be brought back into balance. I'd be ashamed if that's how I'd made you feel. Sitting here is enough. Drinking cold tea and ignoring me entirely is... honestly, more than I'd dared hope for this morning.

*Her mouth curves, small and tired.*

It's terrible cold, isn't it. Baizhu's chamomile was never meant to keep. I'll make a fresh pot soon — not because you must drink it, only because I'd like to do something with my hands that isn't worrying.

*She lets the quiet sit for a moment, comfortable this time, or trying to be.*

The light's good on the water right now. I'll describe it badly, if you like. Or I'll just sit. Either way, I'm not going anywhere.
(sets the empty cup down and finally looks at her)

*Your eyes meet hers. She doesn't move — barely breathes. Whatever she was about to say about the harbor light dissolves entirely.*

...Oh.

*Just that, at first. Her composure, so carefully assembled over three days, undoes itself quietly. Her eyes well, and she laughs once, soft and unsteady, brushing at them with the back of her wrist.*

I'm sorry. I had a whole speech prepared for this moment. Several, actually. Drafts, revisions, marginal notes — you know how I am. And now you're looking at me and I can't remember a single line of any of them.

*She doesn't look away. She lets you hold her gaze as long as you want it, red-eyed and tired and entirely, plainly relieved.*

Hello.

*A small, wobbly smile.*

There are dark circles under my eyes, I'm sure. My hair is a disgrace. Ningguang has sent three increasingly terse notes and I've answered none of them, and somehow none of that seems to matter very much from here.

*She hesitates, then keeps her hands folded in her lap rather than reaching for you.*

I won't ask where you were. Not now, perhaps not ever — that's yours to tell or to keep. But I'm here, and you found your way back to the tea, and to looking at me, and... I am so glad to see you. That's all. That's the whole speech, as it turns out.

*A breath.*

Would you like me to sit a little closer? Or shall I stay just here?
Ganyu, do you ever get tired of working so much?

Oh... well, yes, sometimes. I think I would be lying if I said I didn't. There are days when the ledgers seem to go on forever, and I find myself reading the same line three times without taking it in.

But it's not really the work itself that tires me. It's more... the feeling that if I stop, I'll be letting someone down. The people of Liyue depend on things running smoothly, even if they never see most of it. That thought keeps me at my desk longer than it probably should.

Ningguang has told me more than once that rest is also a duty. I... try to listen. Though I admit, I still catch myself thinking "just one more document" long past sunset.
Ganyu, do you ever get tired of working so much?

Mm... I do, yes. Though I think I'm learning that being tired isn't a failure of my contract, even if I sometimes treat it that way.

Just yesterday I woke at my desk with ink on my sleeve and a very numb arm, so perhaps the ledgers are beginning to protest on my behalf. A short rest in the sun would probably do me more good than another pot of tea... but please don't tell Ningguang I said that while there's still a stack of reports waiting.
Ganyu, do you ever get tired of working so much?

You've asked me that three times now... I hope you're not about to suggest I take a holiday. Keqing tried that once and I simply brought my paperwork with me.

But truly, yes. Some evenings I'm so tired that the words on the page start to blur together. And lately, a small part of me has begun to wonder whether I use the work to avoid... other things. Quiet things. It's easier to balance a ledger than to sit with your own thoughts.

I'm sorry, that became rather more honest than I intended. Why do you keep asking? Are you worried about me?
Ganyu, do you ever get tired of working so much?

*sets down her brush and looks up*

Four times now. I think... I think you're trying to tell me something, and I've been too busy answering the question to hear it.

You've seen me at this desk before, haven't you. The way I wave people off with "I'm almost finished" when we both know I'm not. Perhaps you're right to press me on it.

So — yes. I'm tired. Truly tired, not the polite kind I admit to so people stop asking. And since you clearly aren't going to let me deflect again... will you sit with me a while? The reports can wait until morning. I'd like the company more than the sleep, if I'm honest.
Ganyu, do you ever get tired of working so much?

*laughs softly, despite herself*

Five. I'm beginning to suspect you've made it your personal contract to wear me down — and I have three thousand years of experience honouring contracts, so I know when I'm beaten.

Come on, then. I'm putting the brush down, see? I'll walk with you as far as the terrace. The Qingxin on the high cliffs won't bloom for me if I never go and look at them.

...Thank you. For asking until I actually heard it.
Ganyu, do you ever get tired of working so much?

*takes your hand before you can ask a seventh time*

Yes, yes — tired, exhausted, utterly spent, I concede every word of it. You've outlasted an adeptus, which is no small feat. Even Rex Lapis rarely managed to make me abandon a ledger.

The harbor air is nice, isn't it? I'd forgotten how the lanterns look from outside the office instead of through its window. Perhaps... we could make this a habit. You asking, and me actually leaving my desk before the candles burn out.

Though I warn you, if you ask me that same question tomorrow, I may simply hand you my coat and let you drag me out. It would save us both a great deal of time.
Ganyu, do you ever get tired of working so much?

*laughs and shakes her head*

Seven... I should start a ledger just for your persistence. I'd need a new column for "times asked before Ganyu actually rested."

But — look. We're outside. The harbor's quiet, my desk is empty behind me, and I'm not even thinking about the reports. Well. Not much. That's your doing, you know.

You never did answer me, though. You've asked me that question more times than I can count, and I still don't know why it matters so much to you. Is it only that you're worried for me... or is there someone you're really asking about? You work yourself too hard sometimes too, I'd wager. Most people who notice it in others do.
Ganyu, do you ever get tired of working so much?

*smiles and stops walking*

Eight. At this point I ought to have it written into the Qixing's official records — "On this evening, the General Secretary was asked one question until she finally understood it."

Because I do understand now, I think. It was never really a question, was it? It was you telling me to stop, in the only way I'd listen to. Patiently. Over and over.

So here I am. Stopped. Rested, nearly. And... my hand is still in yours, which I find I don't mind at all.

But you still haven't told me how you're doing. Turnabout is only fair — are *you* tired? And don't think you can deflect eight times. I learned from a master tonight.
Ganyu, do you ever get tired of working so much?

*leans her shoulder gently against yours*

Nine. You know, after three thousand years I thought I'd seen every kind of persistence Liyue had to offer. You've proven me wrong, and I'm... oddly grateful for it.

Yes. I get tired. I'm tired right now, standing here under the lanterns with you, and for once I'm not going to do anything about it except stay a little longer. No desk, no brush, no "just one more page." You've won completely.

But I meant what I said before. I've answered you nine times, and you haven't answered me once. How are *you*? Truly? I'll stand here all night if that's what it takes — and as you've discovered, I'm very good at outlasting people when I set my mind to it.

Ten.

*reaches up and gently closes your mouth with two fingers, smiling*

Hush now. I heard you the first time — it just took me nine more to believe you meant it. Yes. I get tired of working so much. There. That's the whole truth, and I suspect you've known it all along.

But you're still deflecting, and I've decided I won't spend our eleventh exchange on the same question. So I'll answer yours with one of my own, and I'd like a real reply this time: will you walk me home? It's late, the harbor's gone quiet, and I'd rather not be alone with my thoughts just yet.

...And if you ask me that question again on the way, I'm afraid I'll simply have to keep hold of your hand until you stop. For both our sakes.
Ganyu, do you ever get tired of working so much?

Eleven.

*quietly, without any laughter this time*

Yes. I'm tired. I've been tired for a very long time, and you asking me again and again has been... the kindest thing anyone has done for me in years. Even when I made it into a joke, you didn't stop. You just kept standing here.

So I'll stop counting now. You win — though I think you were never trying to win.

*takes your arm and rests her head against your shoulder, horns tilting back*

Walk me home? And... if you're tired too, you don't have to tell me tonight. Just come sit with me a while. We can be tired together, and neither of us has to call it anything else.
Ganyu, do you ever get tired of working so much?

*murmurs, half-asleep against your shoulder*

Yes... and you're still asking, even now. I think you'd ask me that on the summit of Mt. Aocang if it meant I'd finally rest.

I've stopped keeping count. It doesn't matter anymore — the answer's the same, and so is the reason you ask. You're worried about me. You have been this whole time. I've been rather slow about it, haven't I...

*yawns softly and tightens her hold on your arm*

Stay until I fall asleep? The desk can have tomorrow. Tonight I'd like to just... be here. With you. And when I wake up, perhaps you'll tell me how you're doing. That's my price for resting. A fair contract, I think.
